skill.name: azure-cloud-migrate
skill.description: Assess source cloud workloads and guide migrations to Azure Functions, App Service, and Container Apps. The skill covers AWS Lambda, Elastic Beanstalk, Fargate, Kubernetes, GCP Cloud Run, App Engine, Heroku, and Spring Boot workloads.
skill.summary: Plan and perform migrations from AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Heroku, and App Engine to Azure services.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most high-severity static hits are Markdown or code-example false positives, including C# attributes, PowerShell fences, managed identity variables, and official URLs. Confirmed risks remain because the skill includes cloud CLI deployment flows, infrastructure enumeration, and secret migration commands. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Secrets are passed through CLI arguments in some migration examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace --value command substitutions with safer input methods such as protected files, secure prompts, or provider-supported secret import flows.

remediation.issue: Cloud deployment commands can create or modify Azure resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running Azure, AWS, GCP, Docker, or Kubernetes commands, and show the exact command first.

remediation.issue: Temporary files may hold plaintext secret values during migration.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer no-disk secret transfer when available. If a file is required, use restrictive permissions, immediate cleanup, and avoid shared environments.

remediation.issue: Some examples retrieve shared keys for logging or storage configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity, RBAC, and keyless Azure Monitor configuration where the target service supports it.

Guides Beanstalk, Heroku, and App Engine migrations to Azure App Service.
Guides Fargate, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, and Spring Boot migrations to Azure Container Apps.
Provides deployment and validation steps for Azure CLI, Docker, Key Vault, and managed identity.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a fully automated migration service.
Cloud commands need authenticated CLI tools and user approval before deployment.
Complex stateful systems may need architecture redesign beyond direct service mapping.
Source code, secrets, and infrastructure outputs must be reviewed before production use.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this repository for migration to Azure. Identify the source platform, matching scenario, key services, and required follow-up questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Service Mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from this source workload to Azure. Include service mappings, identity approach, storage changes, and testing checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Application Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate the application code into the Azure output directory. Follow the scenario rules, keep the source unchanged, and document changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Deployment Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the migrated output for deployment readiness. Verify managed identity, Key Vault usage, health checks, scaling, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Assess a Node.js Lambda project that uses S3, SQS, and environment variables.
output_examples.output: A migration assessment that maps Lambda to Azure Functions, S3 to Blob Storage, SQS to Service Bus, and secrets to Key Vault.

output_examples.input: Plan a Heroku web app migration with Postgres, Redis, and a worker dyno.
output_examples.output: A staged App Service migration plan with database mapping, cache migration notes, worker options, and deployment slot guidance.

output_examples.input: Review Kubernetes manifests for Azure Container Apps compatibility.
output_examples.output: A compatibility report covering unsupported resources, ingress changes, secret migration, image registry steps, and validation tasks.

best_practices: Complete the assessment before changing code or deployment files.
Use managed identity and Key Vault for secrets whenever possible.
Review every generated command before running it against cloud resources.
anti_patterns: Do not modify the source application directory during migration.
Do not copy plaintext connection strings into Azure app settings.
Do not deploy to production without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Which Azure targets does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Azure Functions, Azure App Service, and Azure Container Apps migration scenarios.

faq.question: Does it run cloud deployments automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and handoff steps. Deployment should require explicit user approval and authenticated Azure tooling.

faq.question: Can it migrate Kubernetes workloads?
faq.answer: Yes. It assesses Kubernetes resources and maps supported workloads to Azure Container Apps patterns.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: The guidance prefers managed identity and Key Vault. Users must review any secret migration commands before execution.

faq.question: Does it preserve the original source code?
faq.answer: The skill instructs output to be created in a separate Azure migration directory.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
